message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether deleting my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch was the right thing to do. Let me start by going through the situation step by step. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom were on a trip. I brought my Switch because I have a long commute to school, and I wanted something to do during the train ride. My stepbrother really liked playing on it, so I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept him occupied while I studied, and it prevented any accidental deletions or changes to my games. When I got back to school, I started getting annoyed because every time I wanted to play a game or go to the eShop, I had to switch back to my profile. It was a minor inconvenience, but it was enough to make me delete his profile. I thought it was no big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, so he wouldn't have access to it anyway. But then, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My stepbrother picked it up and started playing, only to find out his Zelda save was gone. He came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, and started freaking out. When I told him I deleted his profile, he started crying, not full-on, but his eyes were watery and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing on it. So, was it right or wrong to delete his profile? Let me think about the different aspects. On one hand, the Switch is my property. I have the right to manage who uses it and how. I created the profile to keep things organized and prevent any issues with my saves. When I got back to school, the inconvenience of switching profiles each time was enough for me to delete his profile. I didn't think it was a big deal because I don't usually bring the Switch over when I visit. On the other hand, my stepbrother was really into playing on the Switch. He was enjoying it, and when he found out his save was gone, he got upset. My dad thinks it was mean, which makes me consider that maybe I should have communicated better or found another solution instead of just deleting the profile. I guess I didn't think about how much it meant to him. He was using it as a way to pass the time, and losing his progress was upsetting. Maybe I should have talked to him about it before deleting the profile or found a way to keep his saves without the inconvenience of switching profiles. I also didn't consider that bringing the Switch over during Thanksgiving might mean he would want to play again. If I had known I was going to bring it, I might have kept his profile or made a backup of his saves. So, in the end, while I had the right to manage my Switch, not considering my stepbrother's feelings and not communicating with him about the change was probably not the best approach. It led to him feeling upset and my dad thinking it was mean. I should have found a way to balance my needs with his enjoyment of the Switch.
